checks.title: Enforce the selected response to risky identities and sign-ins
checks.statement: Apply separate, effective risk controls for user compromise and risky sign-in events.
checks.prerequisites: Entra policy/risk report read access and licensing for the features assessed; approved test identity for Microsoft-supported risk simulation.
artifacts: Enabled user-risk and sign-in-risk Conditional Access policies
Included/excluded users, grant/session controls and licence coverage
Risk event, policy result and remediation/triage record
steps: Inspect user-risk and sign-in-risk policies separately; identify report-only state, missing resources, broad exclusions and dependence on retiring legacy risk policies.
Declare the expected response for each risk level: block or approved secure remediation. If SCuBA is the chosen target, assess its blocking requirement explicitly.
Use What If plus a Microsoft-supported test-identity simulation where approved; verify the resulting policy decision and operator handling from actual logs.
Confirm workload identities are assessed separately and a remediation flow cannot be completed using only an already compromised password.
checks.expected: The configured response is enforced for each scoped population and matches the explicitly chosen baseline.
checks.limitations: Microsoft supports risk remediation where SCuBA specifies blocking for high risk. Do not report these as equivalent. A risk report alone does not prove enforcement.

checks.title: Restrict security-information registration to approved conditions
checks.statement: Protect the initial registration and replacement of authentication factors.
checks.prerequisites: Authentication-policy and Conditional Access read access; a synthetic new user and managed/unmanaged test devices.
artifacts: Policy targeting the Register security information user action
Approved bootstrap/recovery process and temporary credential settings
Registration audit events and sign-in context
steps: Confirm the registration user action is targeted and that policy state, exclusions and trusted conditions match the approved enrolment design.
Test initial enrolment from approved and unapproved device/location combinations, including the intended bootstrap path for a user who has no factor yet.
Test factor replacement and account-recovery handling for the synthetic user; verify support staff require the approved identity proof.
Trace the resulting factor-change event to monitoring and verify the registered method is the intended one.
checks.expected: Unapproved registration routes fail; legitimate bootstrap and recovery work with controlled proof and an attributable event.
checks.limitations: A compliant-device requirement can deadlock initial enrolment if its bootstrap path is not designed. MFA registration is distinct from MFA enforcement at sign-in.

checks.title: Retire legacy authentication-method policy gaps
checks.statement: Make the current Authentication methods policy the authoritative source for permitted factors.
checks.prerequisites: Authentication-method policy and registration-report reader; test identities for each included/excluded population.
artifacts: Migration state and current method configuration
Per-method targets and exclusions, including passkeys and temporary access passes
Sample registration and sign-in method details
steps: Inspect the migration state and identify any remaining per-user MFA or SSPR policy dependencies; compare them with the current method policy.
Resolve effective eligibility for each enabled method, including emergency and guest users; compare weaker alternatives with the chosen authentication strength.
Using test identities, verify an unapproved method cannot be newly registered and cannot satisfy a phishing-resistant administrative sign-in.
Check approved bootstrap credentials expire as designed and that factor changes are visible to the responsible team.
checks.expected: Effective method availability matches the approved design and weaker alternatives cannot satisfy a stronger access requirement.
checks.limitations: A method being registered does not mean it is allowed for every sign-in. Emergency credentials and guest email OTP need context-specific treatment.

checks.title: Bound application secret and certificate lifetimes
checks.statement: Control application credential creation and expiry while preferring supported secretless authentication.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to application-management policies and credential metadata; dedicated test application with no production permissions.
artifacts: Secret/certificate start/end dates and owners, excluding secret values
Rotation, expiry alert and workload-authentication records
steps: Inventory credential metadata for applications and service principals; identify missing owners, long-lived credentials and near-expiry workload dependencies.
Resolve the effective application-management policy, including per-app overrides and restrictions on new credentials.
In a dedicated test application, attempt an out-of-policy credential lifetime through the normal approved administration process and verify denial; discard test credentials securely.
Inspect a completed rotation and verify the old credential was retired after the replacement was deployed; account for existing credentials that predate the policy.
checks.expected: New credentials obey the selected limits, existing exceptions have treatment plans and rotation does not leave stale secrets active.
checks.limitations: SCuBA specifies particular maximum lifetimes; use those only when that baseline is in scope. A new creation policy may not remediate existing credentials.

checks.title: Verify mailbox audit events and bypass exclusions
checks.statement: Record the mailbox actions needed to investigate owner, delegate and administrator activity.
checks.prerequisites: ExchangeOnlineManagement and Purview audit read permissions; synthetic user/shared mailboxes and approved delegate identities.
artifacts: Organisation AuditDisabled state and mailbox default/custom audit sets
Known mailbox-action events and searchable retention evidence
steps: Check organisation auditing and sampled mailbox audit configuration; inspect owner, delegate and administrator action coverage instead of relying on one AuditEnabled field.
Review audit-bypass associations and custom action lists, including shared mailboxes and applications using delegated access.
Perform benign selected actions in synthetic mailboxes, wait for normal ingestion and retrieve events with actor, mailbox, operation and timestamp.
Verify the event can be found in the central investigation workflow and its retention meets the applicable requirement.
checks.expected: Required actions generate attributable audit records and no unexplained bypass suppresses them.
checks.limitations: Not all actions or mailbox types have identical auditing/licence behaviour. A mailbox-level field alone can misrepresent organisation-level auditing.
checks.command:
Get-OrganizationConfig | Select-Object AuditDisabled
Get-Mailbox -ResultSize Unlimited | Select-Object Identity,AuditEnabled,DefaultAuditSet,AuditAdmin,AuditDelegate,AuditOwner
